method: soil-moisture-triggered irrigation inside the same Wofost72_WLP_FD engine the rainfed regions use: a PCSE StateEvent on SM with zero_condition 'falling', firing when the profile has dried to trigger_depletion_fraction of its plant-available water, i.e. at SM = SMW + (1 - trigger_depletion_fraction) x (SMFCF - SMW) from this region's soils.csv row. The water balance stays live, so a drought still shows a signal here; a potential-production run would erase it. irrigation_amount_cm is a NET application depth in CENTIMETRES: PCSE's water balance reads irrigation_amount as cm (RIRR, cm/day, classic_waterbalance.py) and multiplies it by efficiency. Modelled supply is unconstrained -- no aquifer decline, no allocation limit, no pumping-capacity ceiling in extreme heat -- so the drought protection simulated here is an upper bound, not a forecast of what a well can actually deliver. See README
